sentences.text: 3 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD  AND  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VENKATESH NAIK T  -4-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:18126-DB  MFA No. 100175 of 2015  C/W MFA No. 100176 of 2015  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VENKATESH NAIK T)

These two appeals are filed by the appellants-land losers who are seeking enhancement of compensation challenging the judgment and award dated 01.01.2003 passed in LAC No.56/2002 and the judgment and award dated 17.03.2006 passed in LAC No.57/2001 by the learned II Additional Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Bagalkote (for short 'Reference Court').
2. The appellants are the owners of land bearing Sy.No.56/1B measuring 4 acres 22 guntas and the land bearing Sy.No.56/1A measuring 4 acres 22 guntas situated at Chabbi village, Bagalkote taluk.
The said lands are acquired for the purpose of Upper Krishna Project.
The Special Acquisition Officer calculated the valuation for the year 2008 and awarded a sum of Rs.20,500/- per acre.
Aggrieved by the said award, filed a reference.
On a reference, the Reference Court awarded a sum of Rs.45,000/- per acre.

Learned counsel for the appellants-land losers referring to the judgment passed by the Reference Court disposed off on 22.10.2009 in LAC No.54/2002 submits that the Reference Court awarded a sum of Rs.4,13,820/- per acre for the acquired land bearing Sy.No.53/4A+B situated at Chabbi village, Bagalkote taluk.

4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent-State also referring to the judgment of the Reference Court stated supra submits that the award should be enhanced to Rs.4,13,820/- per acre.

5. Heard the learned counsels for the parties and perused the aforesaid judgment and award.
6.
In the aforesaid judgment the land was acquired under notification dated 15.01.1998.
In the present cases also the lands were acquired under the preliminary notification dated 15.01.1998 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.

sentences.text: 7. Learned Government advocate submits that the lands in these cases and the land in LAC No.54/2002 are of the same village and they are acquired for the same project.

8. Learned counsel for the appellants-land losers also submits that the lands in these cases and the land in LAC No.54/2002 which disposed off on 22.10.2009, are of the same village and acquired for the same project.
9. Submission of learned Government Advocate is placed on record.
10. Following the various judgments, we are of the view that the appellants-land losers are entitled for Rs.4,13,820/- per acre, without any consequential benefits.

11. Accordingly, we pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeals are allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18126-DB (ii) The appellants-land losers are entitled for compensation of Rs.4,13,820/- per acre.
(iii) The respondent shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount within the statutory period.

(iv) In view of the order dated 10.06.2015 in MFA No.100175/2015 and MFA No.100176/2015 passed by this Court, the claimants are not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 4305 and 3134 days respectively in filing the appeals.
(v) The appellants-land losers have to pay the Court Fee for the excess compensation, if not paid.
(vi)Draw modified award accordingly.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18126-DB (vii) Registry is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Reference Court forthwith.
(viii) All pending applications, if any, stand disposed off.

Sd/-
(H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE Sd/-
